blocks.text: Substitution reactions of alkanes take place in the presence of light energy through the formation of highly reactive free radicals. An example is the substitution of a halogen atom with a hydrogen of an alkane, called halogenation. Alkanes react with chlorine and bromine in the presence of sunlight or UV light resulting in the successive replacement of hydrogen atoms with halogens. The extent of halogenation depends upon the amount of halogen used. Reaction of alkanes with fluorine is highly violent and results in a mixture of carbon, fluorinated alkanes and hydrofluoric acid. Iodine does not substitute directly because the reaction is too slow and reversible. The order of reactivity of halogens is:
Halogenation involves the following three steps.
i) Initiation step is the first step in the mechanism of free radical substitution of alkanes by halogens. It involves the breaking of the halogen-halogen bond using energy from the UV light.

blocks.alt: Cl-Cl with two fish-hook arrows from the bond to each Cl, an arrow marked hv, giving Cl. + Cl.
blocks.caption: Initiation step: homolysis of chlorine in UV light (original drawing after the scheme printed on p253 of the textbook).

blocks.text: ii) Propagation step is the second step in the free radical substitution in which the initially formed radicals attack the alkane molecule generating more free radicals.

blocks.alt: Two equations in displayed formulae. CH4 with two fish-hook arrows on one C-H bond + Cl. gives the methyl radical (C with three H and a dot) + H-Cl. The methyl radical + Cl-Cl with two fish-hook arrows on the Cl-Cl bond gives CH3Cl (C with three H and Cl) + Cl.
blocks.caption: Propagation step (original drawing after the scheme printed on p253 of the textbook).

blocks.text: iii) Termination step is the final step in a free radical substitution in which two free radicals react together to form a product. The termination may take place in different ways. The chloride and alkyl radicals may combine to form an chloroalkanes or two chloride radicals may also react to make the chlorine molecule. Another termination mode is the formation of alkane with double number of carbon atoms which takes place when two alkyl radicals merge together. This type of termination is rare and the alkanes with double carbon atoms are formed in traces. However, its presence is evident of free radical substitution mechanism.

blocks.alt: Three termination equations: i) methyl radical + Cl. gives CH3Cl; ii) methyl radical + methyl radical gives ethane, H3C-CH3, with all bonds shown; iii) Cl. + Cl. gives Cl-Cl.
blocks.caption: Termination step: i) to iii) (original drawing after the scheme printed on p254 of the textbook).

blocks.text: By repetition of step (ii), propagation step, a mixture of halogen substituted products (chloroalkanes) is obtained. The more the chlorine gas in reaction mixture to start with, the greater the proportions of chlorine atoms in the chloroalkane molecules formed.
Trichloromethane is also known as chloroform and tetrachloromethane is also known as carbon tetrachloride.

blocks.title: Interesting Information!
blocks.text: Haloalkanes are anaesthetic in nature. The anesthetic power of a haloalkane increases with the number of halogen atoms. Use of these as organic solvents in lab is strictly monitored due to their toxic nature.

blocks.alt: CH3Cl (chloromethane) gives CH2Cl2 (dichloromethane), then CHCl3 (trichloromethane), then CCl4 (tetrachloromethane), with Cl. over each arrow and a red curved arrow over each step labelled Further substitution with Cl. radical.
blocks.caption: Successive substitution of chloromethane to tetrachloromethane (original drawing after the scheme printed on p254 of the textbook).

blocks.title: Quick Check 11.3
blocks.text:
a) Explain why alkanes have high stability?
b) What are major types of reactions that alkanes undergo?
c) How the termination step occurs in the halogenation of alkenes?
d) State the conditions under which a mixture of halogenoalkanes is obtained from the halogenation of alkanes.
e) Predict the products of the free radical chlorination of ethane.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Quick Check 11.3 (c) asks about the halogenation of alkenes; the termination step described in this topic belongs to the free radical halogenation of alkanes.
